findings.title: Division as measured release
findings.claim: The focus frames dividing the Qur'an and sending it down in stages as one sustained delivery for measured recitation to people. Its portions can be read as ordered release, not as a broken or withheld whole.
findings.mechanism: The focus's farraqnahu separates the recitation-object; its purpose clause sends that object into voiced recitation for people, ala makth gives a measured pace, and the n-z-l verb with its cognate noun intensifies staged sending. The wider 25:32 connection sets this process beside an all-at-once demand and links tartil with steadiness; 75:16-19 pairs restraint from haste with gathering, following recitation, and clarification. Together these contacts turn division from mere segmentation into an ordered reception process.
findings.reader_payoff: The portions become a way for one recitable whole to arrive over time and be gathered in the hearer's voice, rather than evidence of a text broken into unrelated pieces.
findings.containment: This describes the focus's stated purpose and does not make every division constructive or guarantee every hearer's reception. The packet also supplies contrary uses: 15:91 treats making the Qur'an into portions adversely, while 3:105 and 2:102 show destructive division. These readings remain alongside the focus's specific pairing of separation with measured recitation and repeated delivery.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface, focus-side branch records, and exact wider Arabic connections ground the delivery relation. The V12/HFT summaries are legacy_unbound nominations, two recitation branch identities remain unresolved, and target morphology is not supplied; those limits qualify the interpretation without erasing its supported core.

findings.title: Staged sending as ordered placement
findings.claim: Alongside repeated delivery, the focus's n-z-l form can also carry a qualified sense of putting the message into a fitting order for recitation.
findings.mechanism: Nazzalnahu tanzilan is the carrier. The focus first divides the object and places its recitation before people at a measured pace; the wider 25:32 connection contrasts all-at-once descent with tartil and steadiness of heart. That contact makes the proper-order branch of n-z-l legible as an arrangement for reception, not delay for its own sake.
findings.reader_payoff: The intervals can be read as a fitting arrangement for receiving the message, while repeated delivery remains the stated foreground.
findings.containment: This does not supply a detailed schedule, prove audience-specific tailoring, or replace the explicit repeated descent. The branch identity is qualified and the fit-to-reception relation is interpretive.

findings.title: Staged disclosure and discernment
findings.claim: The focus's divided, staged message for people can be read alongside wider descriptions of the Qur'an as guidance and criterion and of a sent Book leading people from darkness to light; the delivery can therefore carry an interpretive end in discernment and inward recognition.
findings.mechanism: Farraqnahu carries separation on the focus surface, while n-z-l carries the sending of the Qur'an to people. The 2:185 connection names the sent-down Qur'an as guidance for people, clear proofs, and furqan; 14:1 connects a sent-down Book with bringing people from darkness into light. These wider outcomes meet the focus's division, audience, and staged delivery, shifting graduality from chronology alone toward disclosure that serves recognition.
findings.reader_payoff: The measured portions can be perceived as unfolding guidance toward discernment, not merely as a record of when revelation arrived.
findings.containment: This does not say that farraqnahu lexically means criterion, that every hearer gains inward sight, or that the focus states the causal link explicitly. The target morphology is not supplied; guidance and movement into light are wider contextual triggers, and their link to installment timing remains interpretive.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and the exact wider target Arabic support the guidance, proof, and light imagery. The HFT summary is unanchored, and the movement from those outcomes to the purpose of installment timing is an inference, so the candidate is retained with that boundary visible.

findings.title: Recitation reaches the body
findings.claim: The focus's staged message is meant to be recited to people; a wider scene shows recited signs followed by prostration and tears, letting the delivery be read through an embodied human response.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins sending-down with the act of reciting to an audience. In 19:58, the supplied wider Arabic describes signs being recited and people falling in prostration and weeping. Their shared recitation-to-hearer relation lets the focus's delivery acquire a bodily reception endpoint.
findings.reader_payoff: The movement from revelation to recitation is seen as capable of reaching beyond words into posture and tears.
findings.containment: 19:58 is a wider parallel, not proof that staged delivery causes prostration or that every hearer responds. The refusal in 84:21 remains a counter-reading; humility is inferred from prostration and tears rather than named in the focus.

epistemic.reason: The focus's recitation and audience are explicit, and 19:58 supplies exact Arabic for an embodied response to recited signs. The original summaries are unanchored or tied to same-pericope context, so the wider relation is retained as a qualified parallel rather than a causal claim.

findings.title: Reception is not guaranteed
findings.claim: The focus describes recitation to people, not a guaranteed response: wider passages place prostration and tears after recitation beside a case where people do not prostrate when Qur'an is recited.
findings.mechanism: The focus's recitation-to-people act returns in 19:58, where recited signs are followed by prostration and weeping, and in 84:21, where Qur'an is recited to people who do not prostrate. Their contrasting outcomes make reception a live human response rather than an automatic effect of delivery.
findings.reader_payoff: The audience remains active and varied; delivery can meet response or refusal without either being selected as the universal outcome.
findings.containment: The two wider passages describe separate scenes and audiences. They do not establish that 17:106 causes either response or that the focus predicts what every hearer will do.

epistemic.reason: Exact wider Arabic grounds both response and refusal, while the HFT summary is an unanchored pericope-level synthesis. Only its global, focus-returning reception contrast is retained.
